content.text: Section 8 fully matches the preferred position.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 provides automatic renewal for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal) with a Customer opt-out on only thirty days' written notice, plus a Vendor reminder sixty days before renewal and an extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is late. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. This meets the preferred position on renewal term, notice window, reminder and price cap; the notice obligation runs only against us in a way that is favourable (Vendor cannot force non-renewal), so no redline is warranted. The three-year initial term in 8.1 is an initial commitment, not an auto-renewal term, and is outside this rule.
